title: High-Frequency Polling Queues over General-Purpose Storage
pattern: Services use relational tables or shared disk files as a high-frequency polling message queue, repeatedly scanning and updating state to distribute work among application instances.
why_bad: The polling and state churn create unnecessary database contention, CPU load, index churn, and disk I/O. High-frequency updates and row locking (`FOR UPDATE`) cause lock contention, lock escalation, and deadlocks, and as the table grows, query performance drops off a cliff, leading to thread blocking and cascading failures [273, 274, 565, 566].
detection: Tight or unbounded polling loops that query a queue/status table, frequently locking rows (`FOR UPDATE`) and flipping status columns (e.g., `PENDING`, `DONE`); or loops that repeatedly poll shared files for inter-service work.
counterexample: Ordinary ACID transactional row locking that is transient and not a background-job distribution mechanism; event-driven Change Data Capture logs; dedicated message queues (RabbitMQ, Kafka); deliberately bounded low-throughput database queues whose measured load and transactional requirements justify them.
fix: For the high-frequency contention case, move dispatch to event-driven messaging middleware (e.g., RabbitMQ, Kafka) or suitable CDC-driven delivery, preserving the work's required durability and transaction semantics [530, 562].
source:
*Pragmatic Programmers - Release It! (Nygard), p. 177-178 [273, 274, 565, 566]*  
*Implementing Domain-Driven Design (Vernon), p. 312 [530]*; *Clean Architecture (Martin), Appendix A, p. 326 [732]*
